## 固定收益開篇主論

荷莫茲海峽周邊的運輸干擾再度升高，推動油價大漲；克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack同時表示，恢復物價穩定可能需要不只一次升息。美國公債因而在8月10日遭到拋售，2年期殖利率上升4.7個基點至4.243%，5年期上升6個基點至4.413%，10年期上升6.2個基點至4.708%，30年期則上升5.1個基點至5.253%。這波走勢逆轉了上週五就業報告意外疲弱後的債市漲勢，也使10年期殖利率回到近期拋售行情的高檔區域。

能源是眼前最直接的通膨壓力。伊朗與美國未能就恢復荷莫茲海峽航運取得進展，WTI原油上漲5.01%至$82.10，布蘭特原油上漲4.94%至$87.68。美國總統川普拒絕伊朗索取戰爭賠償的要求，並表示華府準備讓經濟壓力持續累積，而非發動新一輪攻擊。這項立場降低了海峽迅速重開的希望，卻未提供恢復正常商業航運的替代途徑。

美國公債的變動同時反映實質折現率上升與通膨補償增加。10年期實質殖利率上升4.1個基點至2.433%，10年期損益兩平通膨率則上升2.1個基點至2.275%。因此，油價並非只透過通膨預期影響債市。Hammack認為目前利率並未對經濟活動形成實質限制，加上市場仍不確定聯準會將如何因應，也提高了投資人承擔存續期間風險所要求的實質殖利率。

殖利率曲線僅溫和變陡。2年與10年期利差擴大1.5個基點至46.5個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大0.4個基點至101個基點。拋售主要集中在5年與10年期，顯示市場一方面重新納入近期升息風險，另一方面也要求補償可能延續不只一次政策會議的通膨衝擊。30年期殖利率仍高於5.25%，反映財政舉債、龐大企業發債量，以及美國財政部最終將向投資人投放多少長天期債券等長期壓力依然存在。

風險資產承受住利率與油價變動，沒有全面退跌，但市場結構不如上週五就業報告公布後的漲勢穩健。標普500指數近乎持平，那斯達克100指數下跌0.34%，費城半導體指數重挫2.94%。黃金上漲2.69%至$4,457.50，美元指數上升0.19%。投資級債券基金LQD下跌0.55%，HYG與JNK則各跌約0.16%，EMB下跌0.42%。長天期政府債與公司債指數錄得固定收益資產中最大的價格跌幅，與基準殖利率上升相符，並非企業信用風險全面惡化。

本交易日最重要的變化，是勞動市場疲弱一度使市場認為聯準會可以等待之後，通膨與存續期間風險旋即重新浮現。上週五非農就業人數萎縮仍是政策評估的一環，但週一油價反彈與Hammack的談話顯示，就業疲弱本身不足以決定下一步政策。週三公布的消費者物價報告將檢驗勞動與能源訊號究竟是彼此抵銷的衝擊，還是通膨展望更廣泛轉變的開端。

## 油價重新牽動通膨疑慮

荷莫茲海峽未能重新開放，使原本的外交不確定性重新反映於市場價格。布蘭特原油上漲5%，收於$87.68；WTI原油連續三個交易日累計上漲約9%，升至$82.10。伊朗以臨時和平協議遭到違反為由，現階段排除與美國直接談判。川普則表示華府只是在進行部分談判，並暗示伊朗的經濟困境最終可能迫使其改變立場。

雙方的分歧因此不只是時程問題，也涉及和解條件。伊朗與阿曼雖然一直討論海上通行安排，但海峽仍未恢復不受限制的航行。川普反對伊朗在終結衝突的更廣泛協議中要求賠償。市場先前曾因談判取得進展的跡象而作出反應，如今卻仍看不到船東與保險公司能夠恢復正常營運的證據。

其他區域發展進一步加深供給疑慮。胡塞武裝聲稱攻擊了紅海附近的一座沙烏地阿拉伯煉油廠；波斯灣煉油廠受損，以及烏克蘭對俄羅斯工廠的攻擊，原本就已限制成品油出口。中東至中國基準航線的超大型油輪日租金逼近$50萬。即使實體油貨仍可供應，運費上升也會增加能源運抵目的地的成本，因此通膨風險不僅來自原油現貨價格。

能源行情在上週五就業報告之後格外重要。7月非農就業人數減少2.3萬，未如市場預期增加8萬，先前月份的數據也遭下修。最新分析指出，2024年與2025年夏季的就業數據同樣令人失望。僅地方政府就業人數在7月便減少6萬，部分原因是支應教職人員的聯邦補助到期，以及教育工作者季節性退出薪資名冊。

這段歷史使市場仍無法確定，7月數據究竟代表勞動市場持續放緩的開端，還是又一次季節性疲弱。摩根大通經濟學家Michael Feroli表示，如果重演前兩年夏季的情況，未來幾個月數據可能回升。桑坦德銀行經濟學家Stephen Stanley則認為，聯準會在前兩年9月面對類似疲弱時反應過快；由於基礎通膨仍高於目標，這次可能不會過度解讀最新報告。

民間部門的聘僱情況也沒有整體數據所顯示的那麼疲弱。最近三個月民間就業人數平均增加4萬，接近吸收新增勞動力所需約5萬個職位的估計值。這並未否定總就業人數萎縮或先前數據下修，但使政策意涵更具條件性：報告確實顯示勞動市場轉弱，卻未必代表需求崩跌到足以自動壓過能源通膨再起的程度。

Hammack清楚區分了兩者。她是聯準會7月決定將目標利率區間維持在3.5%至3.75%時，主張升息25個基點的三位異議官員之一。她週一表示，單次升息25個基點可能對經濟幾乎沒有影響，或許需要若干次升息，但拒絕預先指定終點。

她的論點立基於當前政策立場，而非僅著眼於油價。Hammack認為目前利率並未實質限制經濟活動，若不採取額外政策行動，通膨恐怕無法回到2%。不過，她也不願預判最終需要調整多少次。這使政策路徑仍取決於數據，同時顯示至少對一位7月的異議官員而言，爭論焦點已是一連串升息，而非是否僅作一次預防性調整。

週一殖利率的組成變化與這項訊息一致。10年期損益兩平通膨率上升2.1個基點，反映能源風險重燃；實質殖利率則上升4.1個基點，幅度接近前者的兩倍。投資人並非只是在上週五的利率結構上加計油價溢價；隨著貨幣政策可能持續收緊的風險回歸，市場也逆轉了就業數據公布後實質利率跌幅的一部分。

## 美國財政部與日本措施面臨政策訊號的侷限

長天期殖利率再度上升，使外界更仔細檢視美國財政部長Scott Bessent試圖抑制主權債市場壓力的作法。投資人將近期多項行動，包括支持美日聯合匯市干預、主張擴大聯準會向外國官方美國公債持有人提供的機制，以及調整再融資聲明措辭，解讀為財政部對長期借款成本相當敏感。

最新市場反應顯示這套作法有所侷限。10年期殖利率升至4.708%，30年期達到5.253%。持續的通膨、每年逼近$2兆的預算赤字，以及隨之而來的債券供給，影響都大於官方溝通方式的改變。財政部可以調整發債期限組合，或降低外國持有人為取得美元而出售美國公債的風險，卻無法單獨帶來足以使投資人接受大幅較低長期殖利率的通膨改善。

不過，財政部把未來標售規模可能「增加」的措辭改為可能「調整」，已經改變市場預期。BMO資本市場的調查顯示，61%的客戶預期下次調整30年期標售規模時會減量而非增量。但財政部尚未宣布減量，目前的再融資時程也維持不變。即使把發債量從殖利率曲線長端移開，也只是將融資需求轉移至其他天期，並不會消除融資需求。

Bessent支持日圓，也有與美國公債市場相關的考量。防止日圓失序貶值，可能減輕日本公債壓力，並降低日本當局為籌措干預資金而出售美國證券的可能性。他提議擴大聯準會的外國與國際貨幣當局附買回機制（FIMA），讓外國央行能以美國公債作為擔保取得更多美元，而不必出售持債。

日本持有超過$1兆的美國公債，但聯準會資料顯示，近期干預期間並未動用這項機制。因此，這項後盾仍是潛在工具，尚未成為本輪行動既有的融資管道。擴大機制也需要聯準會採取行動，並非財政部長可以單方面決定。

日圓走勢呈現更廣泛的限制。日圓週一最多貶值1%，跌破每美元159日圓，抹去7月31日聯合干預所帶來約一半的升幅。美國財政部外匯穩定基金的資產不到$2,200億，日本單是在7月30日的行動估計便動用$530億。聯準會原則上可以提供更大規模的資金，但在美國最近一次行動中，其角色僅限於代表財政部執行買進。

日圓回落反映利差與財政基本面仍未改變。日本央行政策利率為1%，聯準會目標利率區間則為3.5%至3.75%；市場也持續擔心日本的財政計畫與其對進口能源的依賴。在干預效果逐漸消退之際，油價上漲又加重日本的進口成本。每美元160日圓附近仍是重要考驗，因為當局曾於2024年在接近該價位時進場；若匯率持續突破這一區域，可能動搖市場對Bessent廣泛支持承諾的信心。

日本央行週一公布的7月30日至31日會議摘要，向市場傳遞較偏鷹的政策訊號。九位政策委員中，有一位表示基礎通膨正接近2%，若更加重視上行風險，可能有理由以快於市場預期的速度升息。另一位委員則主張，央行應願意考慮更大幅度的調整，而不是固守固定步調。

日本央行7月將利率維持在1%，僅高田創主張立即連續升息。不過，較廣泛的討論顯示，政策重心正從推升基礎通膨，轉向防止其過度超越目標。一位委員表示，央行不能再假設等待的代價微不足道；另一位則指出，目前利率仍低於日本央行估計中性利率區間1.1%至2.5%的下緣。

交換市場定價顯示，9月升息機率約為三分之二，10月前升息則已幾乎完全反映。會議摘要公布後，日圓起初僅小幅變動，隨後在盤中進一步貶值，顯示市場原本已高度預期近期升息，光是討論加速緊縮仍不足以克服既有利差。

日本成長戰略大臣城內實為政府的財政方案辯護，表示為期14年、規模¥370兆的投資計畫，最終將增加市場對日圓資產的需求。他也表示，為期2年、每年成本約¥5兆的消費稅減稅，可透過調整歲入與支出籌措資金。然而，市場仍不清楚投資計畫的公私部門出資比例，使這些保證的即時效果有限。

城內實表示政府尊重日本央行的獨立性，並稱央行表現良好。對一位主張成長的內閣成員而言，這是比投資人可能預期更能接受近期升息的態度。即便如此，週一日圓下跌仍顯示，關於投資與生產力的長期主張，不能取代當前明確的融資計畫，也無法取代美日利差的實質收窄。

美國政策溢價也持續受到制度性問題影響。8月5日的一封信要求聯準會理事Lisa Cook在8月26日前回應白宮的指控；白宮稱她為取得更優惠的房貸條件，不當地將第二棟住宅申報為主要住所。Cook否認有不當行為，也未遭起訴。最高法院6月裁定，她在抗辯罷免行動期間可以繼續留任。隨著市場評估聯準會獨立性，這項法律爭議仍未解決。

國際貨幣基金最新一篇工作論文，為官方關注政府債務的持有結構與融資方式提供歷史背景，但並未證明美國當前措施構成金融壓抑。研究涵蓋17個先進經濟體1920年至2020年的資料，作者估計，透過政策引導銀行持有政府債務或央行負債所產生的財政利益中位數，已由2008年約占GDP的0.08%，增至2020年的0.51%。研究說明了高負債、高利息成本的政府為何可能重視支撐主權債需求的市場機制，也顯示公共融資成本降低，會使銀行、存款人與其他投資人的報酬遭到轉移。

## 企業借款人趕在通膨數據前加速發債

企業借款人利用非農就業報告公布後殖利率短暫下降的機會，趕在本週通膨數據公布前發行異常龐大的債券。週一共有19家投資級發行人出售$276億債券，是1月以來單一交易日借款人數最多的一次。發行人包括公用事業公司、海外銀行與Tyson Foods，為投資人提供的組合比近期許多由金融機構與大型科技公司主導的發債日程更多元。

這波發行延續了8月異常快速的供給步調；8月通常是較為清淡的月份之一。投資級借款人前一週已出售$800億債券，是2026年第三高的單週規模，交易商原本預期本週還會有$400億供給。截至上週五，美國今年高評級債券發行量已達$1.4兆，比2020年同期高出9%。全球聯合承銷公開債券發行量週一達到$5兆，比先前紀錄提早一個多月。

這波搶發同時反映發行人的審慎態度與投資人仍有承接能力。企業希望在CPI與生產者物價數據改變利率展望前完成融資；具吸引力的整體殖利率支撐需求，許多投資級發行人的資產負債表也依然穩健。不過，週一美國公債殖利率上升說明了企業為何選擇迅速行動：即使整體信用環境仍然有序，有利的發債窗口也可能很快收窄。

IBM在美元市場以外完成一筆重要交易，出售C$27.5億、約合$19.7億的4年期與8年期加幣債券，是該公司14年來首次進入Maple債券市場。8年期券的定價較基準高120個基點，略低於初步討論水準；募集資金將用於一般企業用途。外國發行人已推動今年Maple債券發行量創下紀錄。

人工智慧基礎設施持續形成獨立的融資管線。Nvidia宣布與Apollo、Blackstone、BlackRock、Brookfield、Goldman Sachs及KKR合作，涉及$5,000億的AI基礎設施投資。如此龐大的規模加深市場疑慮：Nvidia與科技生態系各方簽訂的協議，可能在強化其晶片需求之餘，也把融資與估值風險集中於彼此相連的公司。

Lambda把這項主題直接帶進槓桿貸款市場。這家獲Nvidia支持的雲端運算業者開始推介一筆$9.17億貸款，資金將用於依照與Nvidia簽訂的合約購買及安裝繪圖處理器與其他基礎設施。初步訂單接近$20億，承諾期限為週四。

擬議條款針對科技資產使用年限較短與再融資風險提供保障。貸款期限為4.4年，短於傳統機構型定期貸款約7年的期限，並將在約4年內全額攤還。發行條件最高為基準利率加375個基點，價格為面額的99美分；結構也包含提前償還罰金，具備較常見於債券的特徵。

全額攤還可降低到期時必須再融資的金額，但也要求相關業務在設備使用期間產生現金。對抵押品可能比傳統工業資產更快淘汰的借款人而言，這項差異格外重要。CoreWeave先前把合約支持的晶片融資引進機構貸款市場，之後卻在另一筆交易支付高出許多的殖利率，顯示成功取得資金並不代表融資成本能夠維持穩定。

Global AI另外取得一筆由摩根大通主導、規模$4.41億的信貸額度。這家成立兩年的公司表示，已簽約營收達$62億，其中$10億已完成建置與交付，並預計在2029年前提供1吉瓦的資料中心容量。自去年以來，全球AI相關債務融資已接近$6,000億，這筆交易再為其增添供給。

監管措施可能進一步拓寬融資管道。美國證券交易委員會工作人員澄清，資料中心資產擔保證券的一個主要類別，不適用於金融資產證券化所須遵守的部分資訊揭露與保障要求。豁免範圍包括風險自留規定，理由是實體資料中心不像貸款或租賃資產池，不會隨時間逐步清償消失。

這項指引並非正式修法，但消除了一項曾影響交易結構的合規障礙。資料中心ABS發行量已由2020年的$24億增至去年的$155億，2026年並有望再創紀錄。不過，這項澄清不適用於以資料中心抵押貸款為擔保的商業不動產抵押貸款證券，後者仍須遵守既有規定。

較寬鬆的待遇可以擴大融資能力，但也使符合資格的交易不再受到全球金融危機後設立的部分保障約束。資料中心業者通常仍承擔可觀的營運曝險，因為評級取決於業者持續持有與管理相關資產。投資人仍須區分這種經濟利益一致性，與法律上必須持有部分已發行債務的要求。

## 重組風險與充裕的初級市場供給形成對比

投資級與AI相關借款人順利籌資之際，巴西石化生產商Braskem卻面臨嚴重壓力。隨著8月24日庭外重組期限逼近，包括Elliott Investment Management與Contrarian Capital Management在內的債券持有人，正要求國營控制的Petrobras作出更明確的財務貢獻。

債權人要求Petrobras透過股權、營運資金或次順位債務提供支持。Petrobras一直有所抗拒，部分原因是持股進一步提高，可能使其必須把Braskem的債務併入自身資產負債表。爭議不僅在於支持金額，也涉及資本結構中哪一層證券應承擔風險。

國際債券持有人提出新的反建議後，Braskem在僅需小幅調整的前提下給予較正面的評價，談判因而有所改善。公司若要採取庭外方案、避免聲請巴西相當於破產保護的司法重整，必須取得至少三分之一債務持有人的支持。若正式提交協議，各方將再獲得90天敲定條款。

Braskem在6月底取得緊急保護，暫停債權人執行權利60天。穆迪隨後將其評級進一步調降至非投資級，並把法院命令的暫緩執行視為違約，同時維持負向展望。Braskem的2030年到期債券，相較同類美國公債的選擇權調整後殖利率溢價約為1,900個基點，遠高於市場通常認定為困境債務的1,000個基點門檻。

交易的政治面向使信用評估更加複雜。Petrobras與IG4 Capital共同控制Braskem，重組期限又落在選舉年。注資可提高協商重組成功的可能性，卻也可能把負債轉向國營控制的股東。Braskem表示，各項提案仍屬意向性質、不具約束力，所有替代方案都仍在考量之中。

公司的營運歷史也加深急迫性。與鹽礦環境災害有關的負債，加上石化產品價格連續多年疲弱，已消耗其現金。這些壓力使Braskem不同於僅想降低成本而尋求再融資的借款人：重組必須同時處理流動性，以及股東與債權人之間的損失分配。

整體初級市場並未呈現同等壓力。即使美國公債殖利率上升，高收益債券基金HYG與JNK當日也僅下跌約0.16%，利率敏感度高出許多的LQD則下跌0.55%。這項比較顯示，基準利率敏感度是投資級債券基金下跌的重要因素，但無法消除個別槓桿科技借款人或Braskem等困境發行人的集中風險。

## 全球通膨訊號使政策路徑分歧

日本偏鷹的政策討論，是全球政策訊號更廣泛分歧的一環。挪威7月基礎通膨意外維持在2.7%，未如預測中位數升至2.9%，也遠低於挪威央行預估的3.3%。數據降低了本週會議升息的機率，也使市場稍微下調9月升息預期。

隔夜交換市場對即將到來的政策決定僅反映2個基點的升息幅度，低於上週五的6個基點；截至9月的定價為15個基點，先前則為17個基點。數據公布後，挪威克朗兌歐元貶值0.1%。Handelsbanken經濟學家認為，這項結果實際上排除了立即升息的風險；不過，國內商品與服務通膨加速，意味著數據尚不能完全解除疑慮。

受電價推動，挪威整體通膨升至3%，高於市場共識的2.8%，但略低於央行預估的3.1%。基礎通膨轉弱、對能源敏感的整體物價卻走強，正反映全球央行面臨的普遍難題：即使政策偏好的通膨指標改善，新的商品衝擊仍可能推高家庭實際感受到的物價。

中國則朝相反方向發展。7月消費者物價通膨由1%降至0.5%，為1月以來最低；生產者物價通膨也由4.1%放緩至3.5%，兩項數據都弱於預期。伊朗衝突使其他地區能源價格維持高檔之際，這些數據提高了全球第二大經濟體再度面臨通膨進一步降溫壓力的風險。

AI相關股票經歷繁榮與反轉後，中國金融監管機關也試圖抑制槓桿。融資餘額在6月底突破人民幣3兆元後，於7月底降至人民幣2.6兆元。中信證券、東方財富等券商加強審查槓桿與衍生性商品帳戶，部分業者限制近期新客戶或反覆接到追繳通知的投資人進一步借款。這些措施旨在維持對具戰略重要性科技公司的支持，同時避免集中槓桿破壞市場穩定。

菲律賓央行面臨更嚴峻的通膨與成長取捨。即使第2季經濟成長意外放緩至2.3%，菲律賓央行總裁Eli Remolona仍表示，央行準備採取必要幅度的緊縮措施，使通膨回到3%的目標。當地通膨率為6.2%，副總裁Zeno Abenoja則表示核心通膨可能已經觸頂。

Remolona承認成長疲弱會減輕升息壓力，但並未認為這足以凌駕物價穩定任務。戰爭引發的通膨打擊家庭消費，涉及防洪基礎建設的貪腐醜聞則削弱投資。央行因此面臨兩難：再次升息可能進一步壓抑已經疲弱的經濟活動，但按兵不動又會讓通膨維持在目標的兩倍以上。

歐元區預測則提供較具韌性的成長訊號。經濟學家將2026年經濟成長預估由0.5%上調至0.8%，主要因為第2季GDP成長0.4%，是預期速度的兩倍。第3季預測仍維持在0.2%，表示這次上修源自已實現的表現，並非每個後續季度的展望都轉強。歐洲正承受能源成本上升、河川運輸不順與製造業壓力，但尚未出現廣泛萎縮，因此這項區別十分重要。

## 市場前瞻意涵

週三公布的美國7月消費者物價報告，是檢驗週一美國公債拋售的首要事件。經濟學家預期整體CPI在6月下降0.4%後，7月將上升0.1%；核心物價預估月增0.2%、年增2.5%，後者將是2月以來最小的核心通膨年增幅。

若結果接近這些預測，將在就業疲弱之外增添基礎通膨放緩的證據，儘管最新一波油價上漲發生得太晚，不會主導已完成統計的7月數據。這將挑戰Hammack所稱若無一連串升息，通膨不太可能回到目標的看法。若數據明顯高於預期，實質殖利率的反彈將更持久，也會重新引發聯準會不能僅因勞動市場疲弱便維持利率不變的疑慮。

價格組成同樣重要。週一10年期名目殖利率上升6.2個基點，其中實質殖利率上升4.1個基點，損益兩平通膨率上升2.1個基點。若核心服務價格轉弱，市場預期所需緊縮程度下降，可能逆轉實質利率的升幅；若物價壓力較為廣泛，則會支持市場即使面對非農就業萎縮，仍同時推高這兩個組成部分的決定。

美國財政部規模$1,250億的再融資標售，將從另一角度檢驗需求。政府預定週二標售$580億3年期公債，週三標售$420億10年期公債，週四再標售$250億30年期公債。10年期標售安排在CPI公布之後；30年期標售則面對高於5.25%的殖利率、龐大企業發債量，以及未來標售規模仍不確定的環境。即使市場預期財政部最終可能減少長債供給，也不會改變本週的標售金額。

在數據日程以外，荷莫茲海峽仍是變化最快的風險。若要出現持久改善，不能只靠另一則談判消息；伊朗、阿曼與美國必須確立哪些船舶可以通行、是否須支付賠償或費用、保險公司是否認為航線具備商業可行性，以及針對能源基礎設施與替代航運路線的攻擊是否停止。在這些條件改變前，油價仍可能使原本較溫和的美國通膨敘事更加複雜。

日圓逼近每美元160日圓，將同時檢驗日本政策與美國支持。若再次干預，市場會以美國財政部外匯穩定基金不到$2,200億的規模、聯準會是否願意投入自身資源，以及FIMA機制是否獲得使用來評估成效。日本央行釋出更強硬的訊號，可提高干預效果的持久性；若利差不變，單靠現貨買進仍將面對曾抹去前次行動一半成果的基本面。

Lambda貸款的承諾期限為週四。最終定價、發行折價，以及是否保留4.4年期全額攤還結構，將顯示接近$20億的初步訂單能否依照擬議保障條款轉化為實際需求。後續資料中心ABS交易則將檢驗，美國證券交易委員會的澄清是否能擴大發行，同時讓投資人繼續區分抵押品、租戶合約、技術使用壽命與發起人曝險。

Braskem的8月24日期限是一項結果更為二元的信用事件。庭外協議需要至少三分之一債權人支持，以及股東團體作出令人滿意的財務貢獻。若無法確定Petrobras的角色與新資本形式，司法重整仍會是替代方案；即使達成協議，各方仍需再用90天敲定條款。2030年到期債券的1,900個基點溢價，已反映市場關注的是回收率與資本結構，而非一般再融資成本。

overall_summary.headline: 荷莫茲航運受阻與聯準會升息風險重燃，美國公債遭拋售並逆轉非農就業報告後的漲勢
overall_summary.session_narrative:
荷莫茲海峽僵局帶動WTI原油上漲5.01%至$82.10、布蘭特原油上漲4.94%至$87.68；先前疲弱的非農就業數據才剛支撐聯準會可以等待的預期，通膨疑慮隨即重燃，美國公債因而遭到拋售。2年期殖利率上升4.7個基點至4.243%，5年期上升6個基點至4.413%，10年期上升6.2個基點至4.708%，30年期則上升5.1個基點至5.253%。

這波走勢不只是反映油價溢價。Hammack表示，目前利率並未實質限制經濟活動，恢復物價穩定可能需要一連串升息；10年期實質殖利率隨後上升4.1個基點，損益兩平通膨率也上升2.1個基點。風險資產未全面退跌，但半導體股明顯走弱，長天期債券基金則錄得固定收益資產中最大的損失。

儘管利率上升，企業融資仍然活躍，19家投資級發行人在本週通膨數據公布前出售$276億債券。週三的CPI報告將檢驗基礎通膨放緩與聘僱疲弱，能否逆轉重新浮現的實質利率溢價，或較廣泛的物價壓力將證明這波拋售合理。
overall_summary.summary: 荷莫茲海峽運輸干擾遲未解決，推升油價與通膨補償；Beth Hammack主張可能需要多次升息，也帶動實質殖利率上揚，美國公債殖利率因而全面走高。週三CPI將檢驗就業疲弱能否使債市恢復非農報告後的漲勢。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries sold off on Aug. 10 as renewed disruption around the Strait of Hormuz pushed oil sharply higher and Cleveland Federal Reserve President Beth Hammack argued that restoring price stability could require more than a single rate increase. The 2-year yield rose 4.7 basis points to 4.243%, the 5-year climbed 6 basis points to 4.413%, the 10-year increased 6.2 basis points to 4.708% and the 30-year added 5.1 basis points to 5.253%. The move reversed the relief that followed Friday’s unexpectedly weak employment report and returned the 10-year yield to its highest area of the recent selloff.

Energy supplied the immediate inflation pressure. WTI crude gained 5.01% to $82.10, while Brent rose 4.94% to $87.68 as Iran and the US failed to make progress toward an agreement that would restore shipping through Hormuz. President Donald Trump rejected Iran’s demand for war compensation and indicated that Washington was prepared to let economic pressure build rather than launch another round of strikes. That stance reduced hopes for a quick reopening without establishing an alternative path to normal commercial traffic.

The Treasury move reflected both a higher real discount rate and greater inflation compensation. The 10-year real yield rose 4.1 basis points to 2.433%, while the 10-year breakeven increased 2.1 basis points to 2.275%. Oil therefore did not act only through expected inflation. Hammack’s judgment that current rates were not meaningfully restraining the economy, together with the continuing uncertainty surrounding the Fed’s reaction function, also raised the real yield investors required to hold duration.

The curve steepened only modestly. The 2s10s spread widened 1.5 basis points to 46.5 basis points, and 2s30s increased 0.4 basis point to 101 basis points. The concentration of the selloff around 5 and 10 years was consistent with a market restoring some near-term tightening risk while also demanding compensation for an inflation shock that could persist beyond a single policy meeting. Thirty-year yields remained above 5.25%, preserving the longer-running pressure from fiscal borrowing, heavy corporate issuance and uncertainty about how much duration Treasury will ultimately place with investors.

Risk assets absorbed the rate and oil moves without a broad retreat, but the composition was less benign than Friday’s post-payroll rally. The S&P 500 finished nearly unchanged, while the Nasdaq 100 fell 0.34% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 2.94%. Gold rose 2.69% to $4,457.50 and the dollar index gained 0.19%. Investment-grade bond fund LQD lost 0.55%, compared with declines of about 0.16% in HYG and JNK and 0.42% in EMB. Long-duration government and corporate bond indices registered the largest fixed-income price losses, consistent with the rise in benchmark yields rather than a uniform deterioration in corporate risk.

The session’s defining change was the reassertion of inflation and duration risk immediately after labor weakness had encouraged expectations that the Fed could wait. Friday’s payroll contraction remains part of the policy calculation, but Monday’s oil rebound and Hammack’s remarks made clear that weak hiring alone will not determine the next step. Wednesday’s consumer-price report now has to decide whether the labor and energy signals represent offsetting shocks or the start of a broader change in the inflation outlook.

## Oil Reopens the Inflation Question

The failure to reopen Hormuz moved from diplomatic uncertainty back into market prices. Brent settled at $87.68 after rising 5%, while WTI reached $82.10 following a gain of about 9% over three sessions. Iran ruled out direct talks with the US for now, citing violations of an interim peace agreement. Trump, meanwhile, said Washington was only partly negotiating and suggested that Iran’s economic difficulties could eventually force a change in position.

The two sides therefore remained separated not merely by timing but by the terms of a settlement. Iran and Oman had been discussing maritime access, yet unrestricted passage through the strait was still unavailable. Trump objected to Iranian demands for compensation in a wider agreement to wind down the conflict. Markets that had previously responded to signs of progress were left without evidence that shipowners and insurers could resume ordinary traffic.

Other regional developments reinforced the supply concern. Houthi militants claimed an attack on a Saudi refinery near the Red Sea, while damage to Persian Gulf refineries and Ukrainian strikes against Russian plants had already constrained exports of refined products. The cost of hiring a supertanker on the benchmark Middle East-to-China route approached $500,000 a day. Those freight costs extend the inflation risk beyond the outright crude price because they affect the delivered cost of moving energy even when physical cargoes remain available.

The energy move mattered particularly after Friday’s employment report. Payrolls fell 23,000 in July rather than increasing by the expected 80,000, and earlier months were revised lower. A new assessment of the release emphasized that summertime employment data had also disappointed in 2024 and 2025. Local-government employment alone fell 60,000 in July, partly reflecting the expiration of federal assistance that had supported teaching staff and the seasonal removal of educators from payrolls.

That history leaves open whether July represents the beginning of a sustained labor slowdown or another seasonal weak patch. JPMorgan economist Michael Feroli said a repeat of the previous two summers could be followed by stronger figures in coming months. Santander economist Stephen Stanley argued that the Fed had responded too quickly to similar weakness in the previous two Septembers and could look through the latest report because underlying inflation remains above target.

Private-sector hiring also looked less severe than the headline. Private payrolls increased by an average of 40,000 over the latest three months, close to an estimate of roughly 50,000 jobs needed to absorb new labor-force entrants. That does not negate the contraction in total payrolls or the downward revisions. It does make the policy implication more conditional: the report showed a weaker labor market, but not necessarily the collapse in demand that would automatically override renewed energy inflation.

Hammack made that distinction explicit. She was one of three officials who dissented from the Fed’s July decision to hold the target range at 3.5% to 3.75%, preferring a quarter-point increase. On Monday, she said one 25-basis-point move would probably have little effect on the economy and that some number of increases could be required, while declining to specify the endpoint.

Her argument rested on the current stance rather than on oil alone. Hammack said interest rates were not meaningfully restricting activity and that she did not expect inflation to return to 2% without additional policy action. The qualification was that she did not want to prejudge how many moves would ultimately be needed. That left the path data-dependent while establishing that, for at least one July dissenter, the debate is about a sequence of increases rather than whether to deliver a single precautionary adjustment.

Monday’s yield decomposition fit that message. The 2.1-basis-point increase in the 10-year breakeven captured the renewed energy risk, but the 4.1-basis-point rise in the real yield was almost twice as large. Investors were not simply adding an oil premium to Friday’s rate structure. They were also reversing part of the real-rate decline that followed payrolls as the possibility of continued monetary restraint returned.

## Treasury and Japan Measures Meet the Limits of Policy Signaling

The renewed rise in long yields intensified scrutiny of Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s attempts to contain pressure in sovereign markets. Investors have interpreted several recent actions—including support for the US-Japan currency intervention, advocacy for a larger Fed facility for foreign official Treasury holders and altered refunding language—as evidence that the Treasury is sensitive to the cost of long-term borrowing.

The latest market response showed the constraints on that approach. The 10-year yield rose to 4.708%, while the 30-year reached 5.253%. Persistent inflation, annual budget deficits approaching $2 trillion and the resulting debt supply remain larger forces than changes in official communication. Treasury can alter the maturity mix of issuance or reduce the risk that a foreign holder sells securities to obtain dollars, but it cannot by itself supply the inflation improvement required for investors to accept materially lower long-term yields.

The department’s replacement of possible future auction “increases” with possible future “changes” has nevertheless shifted expectations. In a BMO Capital Markets survey, 61% of clients anticipated that the next adjustment in 30-year auction sizes would be a reduction rather than an increase. No reduction has been announced, and the current refunding schedule remains intact. Moving issuance away from the long end would also transfer financing needs elsewhere on the curve rather than eliminate them.

Bessent’s support for the yen has a related Treasury-market purpose. Preventing disorderly depreciation could reduce pressure on Japanese bonds and lessen the possibility that Japanese authorities sell US securities to finance intervention. His proposal to enlarge the Fed’s Foreign and International Monetary Authorities Repo Facility would give foreign central banks more capacity to raise dollars against Treasuries instead of liquidating them.

Japan has more than $1 trillion of Treasury holdings, but Fed data showed no use of the facility during the recent intervention. The backstop therefore remains a potential instrument rather than an established funding channel for the current campaign. Its expansion would also require action by the Fed, placing it beyond the Treasury secretary’s unilateral control.

The yen’s performance demonstrated the broader limitation. It weakened as much as 1% on Monday, fell beyond 159 per dollar and erased about half the gains generated by the July 31 joint intervention. The Treasury’s Exchange Stabilization Fund holds less than $220 billion, while Japan alone was estimated to have spent $53 billion on its July 30 operation. The Fed could in principle provide greater capacity, but its role in the latest US operation was limited to conducting purchases on Treasury’s behalf.

The currency’s retreat reflected persistent rate and fiscal fundamentals. The BOJ’s policy rate is 1%, against the Fed’s 3.5%-to-3.75% target range, and markets remain concerned about Japan’s fiscal plans and dependence on imported energy. Higher oil prices add to the country’s import bill just as the intervention effect fades. The 160-per-dollar area remains an important test because authorities intervened near that level in 2024 and another sustained breach could challenge the credibility of Bessent’s expansive pledge of support.

Monday’s summary of the BOJ’s July 30-31 meeting gave the market a more hawkish policy signal. One of the nine board members said underlying inflation was approaching 2% and that greater attention to upside risks could justify raising rates faster than markets expected. Another argued that the bank should be willing to consider larger moves rather than adhere to a fixed pace.

The BOJ held its rate at 1% in July, and only Hajime Takata called for an immediate consecutive increase. The broader discussion nevertheless showed that the policy focus is shifting from lifting underlying inflation to preventing it from moving too far above target. One member said the bank could no longer assume that the cost of waiting was marginal, while another noted that the current rate remained below the lower end of the BOJ’s estimated neutral range of 1.1% to 2.5%.

Swaps assigned about a two-thirds probability to a September increase and almost fully priced a move by October. The yen moved only modestly after the summary before extending its decline later in the session, indicating that expectations of a near-term move were already substantial and that a discussion of faster tightening was insufficient to overcome the existing rate gap.

Growth Strategy Minister Minoru Kiuchi defended Japan’s fiscal program and said the government’s ¥370 trillion investment plan over 14 years would ultimately increase demand for yen-denominated assets. He also argued that a 2-year sales-tax reduction costing about ¥5 trillion annually could be financed through changes in revenue and expenditure. Markets still lack a division between public and private funding for the investment plan, limiting the immediate value of those assurances.

Kiuchi said the government respected BOJ independence and described the bank as doing a good job, a softer stance toward near-term tightening than investors might have expected from a pro-growth cabinet member. Even so, Monday’s currency decline showed that long-run claims about investment and productivity do not substitute for a current funding plan or a decisive narrowing of the rate differential.

Institutional questions also remain present in the US policy premium. An Aug. 5 letter gave Fed Governor Lisa Cook until Aug. 26 to respond to the White House’s allegations that she improperly identified a second home as her primary residence to obtain better mortgage terms. Cook has denied wrongdoing and has not been charged. The Supreme Court ruled in June that she could remain in office while contesting an attempt to remove her, leaving the legal dispute unresolved as markets assess the Fed’s independence.

A new IMF working paper provides historical context for the official interest in the ownership and financing of government debt, without establishing that current US measures constitute financial repression. Studying 17 advanced economies from 1920 through 2020, the authors estimated that the median fiscal benefit from policies directing banks toward government debt or central-bank liabilities increased from about 0.08% of GDP in 2008 to 0.51% in 2020. The research underscores why governments with high debt and interest costs may focus on the plumbing that supports sovereign demand, while also showing that cheaper public financing transfers returns away from banks, depositors and other investors.

## Corporate Borrowers Accelerate Ahead of Inflation Data

Corporate borrowers used the brief post-payroll decline in yields to bring an unusually large volume of bonds before this week’s inflation reports. Nineteen investment-grade issuers sold $27.6 billion of debt on Monday, the largest number of borrowers in a single session since January. Utilities, overseas banks and Tyson Foods were among the issuers, giving investors a broader mix than the financial institutions and large technology companies that have dominated many recent calendars.

The session extended an exceptional pace for August, normally one of the quieter months. Investment-grade borrowers sold $80 billion in the preceding week, the third-highest weekly total of 2026, and dealers had expected another $40 billion for the current week. As of Friday, US high-grade issuance for the year had reached $1.4 trillion, 9% ahead of the comparable 2020 pace. Global syndicated public-bond issuance reached $5 trillion on Monday, more than a month earlier than the previous record.

The rush reflects both issuer caution and continuing investor capacity. Companies sought to complete financing before CPI and producer-price data could change the rate outlook. Attractive all-in yields have supported demand, while many investment-grade issuers retain strong balance sheets. Monday’s rise in Treasury yields nevertheless illustrates why borrowers are choosing to move quickly: a hospitable issuance window can narrow even when broad credit conditions remain orderly.

IBM added a significant transaction outside the US dollar market. It sold C$2.75 billion, or about $1.97 billion, of 4- and 8-year Canadian bonds in its first Maple-market issue in 14 years. The 8-year tranche priced 120 basis points above its benchmark, slightly tighter than initial discussions, and proceeds were designated for general corporate purposes. Foreign issuers have already driven annual Maple issuance to a record.

Artificial-intelligence infrastructure continued to create its own financing pipeline. Nvidia announced a partnership with Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR involving $500 billion of AI infrastructure investment. The scale added to concern that Nvidia’s agreements throughout the technology ecosystem may reinforce demand for its chips while also concentrating financing and valuation risk among connected companies.

Lambda brought that theme directly into leveraged loans. The Nvidia-backed cloud-computing provider began marketing a $917 million loan to finance the purchase and installation of graphics processors and other infrastructure under a contract with Nvidia. Preliminary orders approached $2 billion, with commitments due Thursday.

The proposed terms contain protections designed for the short useful life and refinancing risk of technology assets. The loan has a 4.4-year maturity, compared with roughly 7 years for a conventional institutional term loan, and will amortize fully over approximately 4 years. It was offered at as much as 375 basis points above the benchmark rate and 99 cents on the dollar. The structure also includes an early-redemption penalty, giving it features more commonly associated with bonds.

Full amortization reduces the amount that must be refinanced at maturity, but it also requires the underlying business to generate cash while the equipment is being used. That distinction is important for a borrower whose collateral can become obsolete faster than traditional industrial assets. CoreWeave previously introduced contract-backed chip financing to the institutional loan market and later paid a substantially higher yield on another transaction, demonstrating that market access does not guarantee stable funding costs.

Global AI secured a separate $441 million credit facility led by JPMorgan. The 2-year-old company said it had $6.2 billion of contracted revenue, including $1 billion already built and delivered, and expected to make 1 gigawatt of data-center capacity available by 2029. The financing adds to nearly $600 billion of AI-related debt raised globally since last year.

Regulation may broaden the channels for that borrowing. SEC staff clarified that a major category of data-center asset-backed securities is not subject to certain disclosures and protections applied to securitizations of financial assets. The relief includes risk-retention requirements because the physical data centers, unlike pools of loans or leases, do not liquidate over time.

The guidance is not a formal rule change, but it removes a compliance obstacle that had influenced transaction structures. Data-center ABS issuance increased to $15.5 billion last year from $2.4 billion in 2020 and was on course for another record in 2026. The clarification does not extend to commercial mortgage-backed securities secured by data-center mortgages, which remain subject to the existing requirements.

Easier treatment can expand financing capacity, but it also removes protections created after the global financial crisis from eligible transactions. Data-center operators generally retain substantial operating exposure because ratings depend on their continued ownership and management of the assets. Investors must still distinguish that economic alignment from a legal requirement to retain part of the issued debt.

## Restructuring Risk Contrasts With Abundant Primary Supply

The ease with which investment-grade and AI-linked borrowers raised capital contrasted with acute stress at Brazilian petrochemical producer Braskem. Bondholders including Elliott Investment Management and Contrarian Capital Management were pressing state-controlled Petrobras to make a firmer financial contribution as an Aug. 24 deadline approached for an out-of-court restructuring.

Creditors were seeking support through equity, working capital or junior debt. Petrobras had resisted, partly because a larger ownership position could require it to consolidate Braskem’s debt on its own balance sheet. The dispute concerns not only the amount of support but also which security in the capital structure should absorb the risk.

Negotiations improved after international bondholders presented a new counterproposal that Braskem viewed more favorably, subject to minor adjustments. The company needs support from holders of at least one-third of its debt to pursue an out-of-court solution and avoid filing for judicial recovery, Brazil’s equivalent of bankruptcy protection. If an agreement is filed, the parties would receive another 90 days to finalize terms.

The company obtained emergency protection in late June that suspended creditor enforcement for 60 days. Moody’s subsequently downgraded Braskem farther into junk and treated the court-ordered standstill as a default, retaining a negative outlook. Braskem’s 2030 bonds traded at an option-adjusted yield premium of roughly 1,900 basis points over comparable Treasuries, well beyond the 1,000-basis-point level commonly associated with distressed debt.

The transaction’s political dimension complicates the credit assessment. Petrobras controls Braskem with IG4 Capital, and the deadline falls during an election year. A capital injection could improve the prospects for a consensual restructuring, but it could also shift liabilities toward a state-controlled shareholder. Braskem said the proposals remained indicative and nonbinding and that all alternatives were under consideration.

The company’s operating history adds to the urgency. Cash has been depleted by liabilities related to an environmental disaster at a salt mine and by several years of weak petrochemical pricing. Those pressures distinguish the case from a borrower merely seeking to refinance at a lower cost: the restructuring must address both liquidity and the distribution of losses among shareholders and creditors.

The broader primary market did not show comparable stress. High-yield bond funds HYG and JNK fell only about 0.16% on the day despite higher Treasury yields, while the much longer-duration LQD lost 0.55%. The comparison suggests that benchmark-rate sensitivity contributed substantially to the investment-grade fund decline. It does not resolve the concentration of risk in individual leveraged technology borrowers or distressed issuers such as Braskem.

## Global Inflation Signals Pull Policy Paths Apart

Japan’s hawkish discussion was part of a wider divergence in global policy signals. In Norway, underlying inflation unexpectedly held at 2.7% in July rather than rising to the 2.9% median forecast and remained well below Norges Bank’s 3.3% projection. The result reduced the probability of an increase at this week’s meeting and slightly lowered expectations for September.

Overnight swaps priced only 2 basis points of tightening for the imminent decision, down from 6 basis points on Friday, and 15 basis points by September, compared with 17 basis points previously. The krone weakened 0.1% against the euro after the release. Economists at Handelsbanken judged that the result effectively removed the risk of an immediate increase, although domestic goods-and-services inflation accelerated and prevented the data from becoming an all-clear.

Headline Norwegian inflation rose to 3% because of electricity costs, above the 2.8% consensus but just below the central bank’s 3.1% forecast. The split between weaker underlying inflation and firmer energy-sensitive headline prices resembles the broader global problem confronting central banks: the desired measure can improve even while a new commodity shock raises the prices households see.

China moved in the opposite direction. Consumer-price inflation slowed to 0.5% in July from 1%, the weakest rate since January, while producer-price inflation moderated to 3.5% from 4.1%. Both readings were weaker than expected. The figures increased the risk that disinflationary pressure would re-emerge in the world’s second-largest economy even as the Iran conflict kept energy prices elevated elsewhere.

Chinese financial regulators were also trying to contain leverage after a boom and reversal in AI-related equities. Margin balances fell to 2.6 trillion yuan at the end of July after exceeding 3 trillion yuan in late June. Brokerages including Citic Securities and East Money raised scrutiny of leverage and derivatives accounts, with some restricting further borrowing by recent clients or investors receiving repeated margin calls. The measures were aimed at preserving support for strategically important technology companies without allowing concentrated leverage to destabilize markets.

The Philippine central bank faced a more severe inflation-growth trade-off. Governor Eli Remolona said the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas was prepared to tighten as much as necessary to restore inflation to its 3% target, even after economic growth slowed unexpectedly to 2.3% in Q2. Inflation was running at 6.2%, while Deputy Governor Zeno Abenoja said core inflation might have plateaued.

Remolona acknowledged that weaker growth reduced the pressure to tighten, but did not treat it as overriding the price-stability mandate. Household consumption has been damaged by war-driven inflation, while investment has been weakened by a corruption scandal involving flood infrastructure. The result is a policy choice in which another increase could restrain already-soft activity, but a hold would leave inflation at more than twice the target.

Forecasts for the euro area offered a more resilient growth signal. Economists raised their 2026 expansion estimate to 0.8% from 0.5%, mainly because Q2 GDP grew 0.4%, twice the expected pace. Forecasts for Q3 remained at 0.2%, indicating that the revision reflected completed performance rather than a stronger outlook for every subsequent quarter. The distinction matters as Europe absorbs higher energy costs, weak river transport and pressure on manufacturing without yet showing a broad contraction.

## Forward Market Significance

Wednesday’s July US consumer-price report is the immediate test of Monday’s Treasury selloff. Economists expect headline CPI to rise 0.1% after a 0.4% decline in June. Core prices are projected to increase 0.2% on the month and 2.5% from a year earlier, which would be the smallest annual core increase since February.

A result near those forecasts would add evidence of underlying moderation to the weaker employment picture, even though the latest oil rally occurred too late to define the completed July data. It would challenge Hammack’s contention that inflation is unlikely to return to target without a sequence of increases. A material upside surprise would make the real-yield rebound more durable and revive concern that the Fed cannot treat labor weakness as sufficient reason to remain on hold.

The composition will matter because Monday’s 6.2-basis-point increase in the 10-year nominal yield combined a 4.1-basis-point rise in the real yield with a 2.1-basis-point increase in the breakeven. Softer core services could reverse the real-rate portion by reducing the expected need for restraint. Broader price pressure would validate the market’s decision to raise both components despite the payroll contraction.

Treasury’s $125 billion refunding sequence provides a separate test of demand. The government is scheduled to sell $58 billion of 3-year notes on Tuesday, $42 billion of 10-year notes on Wednesday and $25 billion of 30-year bonds on Thursday. The 10-year auction follows CPI, while the 30-year sale confronts a yield above 5.25%, heavy corporate issuance and continuing uncertainty over future auction sizes. Expectations that Treasury might eventually reduce long-bond supply do not alter the amount offered this week.

Hormuz remains the fastest-moving risk beyond the data calendar. A durable change requires more than another report of negotiations: Iran, Oman and the US must establish which ships can pass, whether compensation or fees apply, whether insurers regard the route as commercially usable and whether attacks on energy infrastructure and alternative shipping corridors cease. Until those conditions change, oil can continue to complicate an otherwise softer US inflation narrative.

The yen’s approach toward 160 per dollar will test both Japanese policy and US support. Another intervention would be judged against the less-than-$220 billion size of the Treasury’s Exchange Stabilization Fund, the Fed’s willingness to participate with its own resources and any use of the FIMA facility. A stronger BOJ signal could improve the durability of intervention; spot purchases without a change in the rate differential would again face the fundamentals that erased half of the previous move.

Lambda’s loan commitments are due Thursday. Final pricing, the issue discount and retention of the 4.4-year fully amortizing structure will show whether preliminary orders near $2 billion translate into demand at the proposed protections. Subsequent data-center ABS transactions will test whether the SEC’s clarification expands issuance while investors continue to differentiate among collateral, tenant contracts, technological life and sponsor exposure.

Braskem’s Aug. 24 deadline presents a more binary credit event. An out-of-court agreement requires at least one-third creditor support and a satisfactory contribution from the shareholder group. Failure to settle the role of Petrobras and the form of new capital would preserve judicial recovery as an alternative, while an agreement would still leave another 90 days to finalize terms. The 1,900-basis-point premium on the 2030 bonds already reflects a market focused on recoveries and capital structure rather than ordinary refinancing cost.

section_summaries.market_read: The selloff restored both near-term tightening risk and compensation for an inflation shock that could persist beyond one meeting.
section_summaries.summary: The 10-year yield rose 6.2 basis points to 4.708%, with both real yields and breakevens higher as the Hormuz impasse lifted oil and Hammack argued that restoring price stability may require a sequence of rate increases. The move reversed Friday’s labor-driven relief, while modest curve steepening and losses concentrated in longer-duration bond funds pointed to repricing of inflation and duration risk rather than a broad credit retreat.

section_summaries.market_read: The larger rise in the 10-year real yield than in the breakeven showed that investors restored a monetary-restraint premium as well as energy risk.
section_summaries.summary: The Hormuz impasse returned directly to energy prices: Iran ruled out direct US talks for now, Trump rejected compensation demands, and ordinary shipping access remained unresolved as refinery attacks and freight costs added supply pressure. July payrolls fell 23,000, but seasonal weakness and steadier private hiring made the labor signal less decisive. Hammack said rates were not meaningfully restrictive and that more than one increase could be needed.

section_summaries.market_read: Communication and funding backstops can change market plumbing, but they cannot replace lower inflation or a narrower US-Japan rate gap.
section_summaries.next_check: A sustained move through 160 per dollar would test the durability of Japanese intervention and US support.
section_summaries.section_title: Treasury and Japan Measures Meet the Limits of Policy Signaling
section_summaries.summary: Official efforts to ease sovereign-market pressure met hard limits: deficits near $2 trillion, inflation and debt supply kept long yields elevated despite softer Treasury auction language and a proposed FIMA expansion. The yen weakened beyond 159 per dollar as the rate gap and fiscal doubts outweighed a more hawkish BOJ discussion. No 30-year auction cut has been announced, and the repo backstop was unused in the recent intervention.

section_summaries.market_read: Strong demand preserves financing capacity, but short-lived technology collateral makes amortization, contracts and refinancing costs decisive.
section_summaries.next_check: Thursday’s Lambda commitments will test demand for the proposed pricing, discount and fully amortizing structure.
section_summaries.section_title: Corporate Borrowers Accelerate Ahead of Inflation Data
section_summaries.summary: Nineteen investment-grade issuers sold $27.6 billion before inflation data, extending an exceptional August supply pace as borrowers used the brief post-payroll decline in yields. AI financing also expanded: Lambda marketed a $917 million, 4.4-year fully amortizing loan, while Global AI secured $441 million and SEC guidance eased a compliance obstacle for eligible data-center ABS.

section_summaries.market_read: Braskem’s depleted liquidity and environmental liabilities make recoveries and loss allocation more important than ordinary refinancing cost.
section_summaries.next_check: The Aug. 24 deadline will show whether Petrobras support and one-third creditor approval can avert judicial recovery.
section_summaries.section_title: Restructuring Risk Contrasts With Abundant Primary Supply
section_summaries.summary: Braskem bondholders pressed Petrobras for equity, working capital or junior debt before the Aug. 24 restructuring deadline. A more favorable counterproposal improved negotiations, but an out-of-court solution still requires support from at least one-third of creditors and agreement on shareholder funding. The roughly 1,900-basis-point premium on Braskem’s 2030 bonds contrasted with orderly broader credit markets and abundant primary issuance.

section_summaries.next_check: This week’s Norges Bank decision will show whether softer underlying inflation outweighs firmer headline prices.
section_summaries.section_title: Global Inflation Signals Pull Policy Paths Apart
section_summaries.summary: Norway’s underlying inflation held at 2.7%, reducing near-term tightening expectations even as headline inflation rose with electricity costs. China’s consumer and producer inflation weakened, reviving disinflation risk, while regulators curbed leverage after an AI-equity boom. The Philippines faced the opposite problem, with 6.2% inflation against 2.3% Q2 growth, and euro-area forecasts improved after stronger completed Q2 activity.

July CPI is the immediate test of whether softer employment and underlying inflation can reverse Monday’s rise in real yields or whether broader price pressure sustains it. Treasury’s $125 billion refunding will separately test duration demand, while a durable Hormuz reopening requires commercially usable passage rather than another report of negotiations. Yen intervention, Lambda’s loan and Braskem’s restructuring remain additional event-specific tests.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries sell off as oil disruption and renewed Fed tightening risk reverse post-payroll relief
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries sold off as the Hormuz impasse sent WTI up 5.01% to $82.10 and Brent up 4.94% to $87.68, reviving inflation concerns just after weak payrolls had supported expectations that the Fed could wait. The 2-year yield rose 4.7 basis points to 4.243%, the 5-year climbed 6 basis points to 4.413%, the 10-year increased 6.2 basis points to 4.708% and the 30-year added 5.1 basis points to 5.253%.

The move reflected more than an oil premium. The 10-year real yield rose 4.1 basis points and the breakeven increased 2.1 basis points after Hammack said current rates were not meaningfully restrictive and restoring price stability could require a sequence of increases. Risk assets avoided a broad retreat, but semiconductor shares weakened sharply and longer-duration bond funds sustained the largest fixed-income losses.

Corporate financing remained active despite the rate rise, with nineteen investment-grade issuers selling $27.6 billion before this week’s inflation data. Wednesday’s CPI report will test whether underlying moderation and softer hiring can reverse the renewed real-rate premium or whether broader price pressure validates the selloff.
